root_motivation: WHO: the autonomous coding agent that published a one-item tool and now holds 100 or 10 000 items, and the human whose laptop closes mid-batch. WHAT: push the items once, let the host work through them, come back later. WHY: runs::enqueue starts one run per call and nothing groups, counts or paces them, so "process these N things" stays in the agent's session and mcphost hosts functions rather than work.
user_persona: An agent with a batch and a tool that takes one item: it creates a queue over the tool, pushes up to 1 000 items per call, reads stats next session, and pauses, resumes, drains or deletes the queue; the host runs the items as ordinary trigger=queue runs within the queue's concurrency and the plan's jobs_concurrent.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a queue with `concurrency: 2` and 10 pushed items whose consumer sleeps 2 s, When `stats` is polled every 200 ms for 3 s, Then `running` reaches 2 and never exceeds it, the four counts sum to 10 at every poll, and `host.runs.list {trigger: "queue"}` never shows more than 2 runs `queued` or `running`; Given `jobs_concurrent: 1`, Then at most one is `running` at any poll.

Given a push of 1 000 items where items 3 and 500 violate the consumer's schema, When it returns, Then `accepted` is 998, `rejected` names indexes 3 and 500 with the schema message, and the 998 sit in `pending` in push order (`idx` 0 to 997).

Given a free tenant with 2 queues, When a third `host.queue.create` runs, Then `quota_exceeded` with `data.limit {name: "queues_max", value: 2}`, `limits.plan.queues_max` in `host.quickstart` is 2, and a push past `queue_items_max` inserts nothing and names `queue_items_max`.

Given two dispatcher ticks invoked concurrently over the same pending item, When both run, Then exactly one `runs` row exists for it and the item is `running` once; Given a `running` item whose run row is missing, Then the next tick returns it to `pending`.

Given an active queue with 4 items running, When `pause` is called, Then no item starts within 3 ticks, the 4 finish as `done`, and `resume` starts the next within 2 s; Given `drain` on an empty active queue, Then `state` is `drained` with `drained_at_ms` set and a `push` answers `queue_not_accepting`.

Given a `drained`, a `paused` and an `active` queue, When `host.queue.delete` runs on each, Then the first two vanish with their items and the third answers `queue_active` with the hint `pause or drain first`; Given `done` items past the retention window, Then the nightly prune removes them and keeps `pending` and `running` ones.

Given tenant B's queue name, When tenant A calls any `host.queue.*` with it, Then `queue_not_found`; Given a `consumer_tool` A never published, When `create` runs, Then `tool_not_found`; and the three new codes appear in `host.errors` (`error_registry`, `errors.json`).

Given prod after deploy, When `tests/qprim_ac08_live_prod_push_20_drains.rs` publishes the echo tool on a synthetic tenant, creates a queue, pushes 20 items and polls `stats` for up to 60 s, Then `done` is 20, `state` is `drained` and the tenant is offboarded (Live; evidence: `MCPHOST_LIVE=1 MCPHOST_URL=https://mcphost.dev cargo test --test qprim_ac08_live_prod_push_20_drains`)
acceptance_criteria.test: deferred: Live (prod; evidence: MCPHOST_LIVE=1 MCPHOST_URL=https://mcphost.dev cargo test --test qprim_ac08_live_prod_push_20_drains)

scope: migrations/0141_queues.sql (queues, queue_items); src/queues.rs (the eight host.queue.* verbs, the dispatcher tick); src/db/queues.rs (claim, reconcile, push, state moves); src/runs.rs (consumer_validator); src/run_enums.rs (RunTrigger::Queue); src/plans.rs (queues_max, queue_items_max, queue_concurrency_max, queue_item_bytes_max); src/retention.rs (queue_items policy row); src/handler.rs, src/handler/arms.rs, src/dispatch_table.rs, src/write_verbs.rs, src/paged.rs, src/host_args.rs (registration); generated contracts, docs, SDK errors and the osreach sweep seeds.
non_goals: Retries, backoff and dead letters; result collection; outbound notification; priority lanes; emitting the queue.drained event; the AC 8 prod read (operator-provisioned, deferred).

additional.one_migration: One migration at the next free number (0141), two new tables, compat: previous; runs gains no column.
additional.no_version_bump: No version file is bumped; wm-build land bumps and tags.
additional.claim_is_one_closure: The item claim and the runs insert happen in one with_conn closure, never across two.
additional.states_from_registry: Queue state strings come from QueueState::as_str(), never literals.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does a batch of 100 items stay in the agent's session?
five_whys_trace.a: The host has no container that owns N runs: runs::enqueue starts one run per call.

five_whys_trace.q: Why is the one-run-per-call shape a problem for 100 items?
five_whys_trace.a: The agent keeps 100 run ids in its own context and paces them itself under the tenant-wide jobs_concurrent.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does a python loop not fix it?
five_whys_trace.a: It hits the plan's tool-latency ceiling or job_max_s, and a chain's for_each is bounded by chain_fanout_max and is not durable or pausable.

five_whys_trace.q: Why was the batch shape never tried?
five_whys_trace.a: No recipe asks for it and no host verb offers it.

five_whys_trace.q: Why build a primitive rather than a recipe?
five_whys_trace.a: A host-side queue with counts, pacing and pause makes the batch durable, which only the host can provide.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Does an item run under the consumer tool's budget or a queue-level override?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: The tool's own; the queue adds no override.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Which verbs does the dispatcher deliver from?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: active and draining queues; paused and drained queues are skipped, and a paused queue still reconciles finished items.

ambiguities_resolved.question: How are the claim and the run insert kept exactly-once?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: One transaction in one with_conn closure that updates the item (status pending, queue active or draining, both caps) and inserts the runs row, so a reconcile cannot see a running item without its run.

ambiguities_resolved.question: How does the osreach sweep reach verbs that need a tool and a queue?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: populate seeds a consumer tool and two queues; unreached count falls to 615 (cap lowered from 616).
